key_insight: LLM agents can sometimes convert general reasoning into reusable, low-cost artifacts, but strong zero-shot accuracy does not reliably predict successful "bottling."
engineering_relevance: For large repeated workloads, the key design problem is not just model quality but whether an agent can spend limited budget to build a cheaper solution that still preserves most of the performance.
method: Introduces BOTTLED, a benchmark where agents receive an unlabeled workload and must solve it under fixed time, compute, and API budgets.
Allows agents to choose the bottling strategy, such as training a small model or writing a reusable program.
Compares bottled solutions against zero-shot LLM performance and small-model distillation baselines across ten models and three tasks.
evidence_signal: Across 60 bottling runs, 48 fell below the lower bound of the model’s zero-shot 95% confidence interval, and 31 underperformed the stronger of two distillation baselines with the same token budget.
watch_item: Bottling gains depend heavily on task structure and budget assumptions, so results may not transfer directly to workloads with different repetition patterns or deployment constraints.
paper_title: Agent in a Bottle: Can LLM Agents Turn Their Capabilities Into Cheap, Scalable Artifacts?
